brief:
Today, 18 November, is a rest day on the plan. You trained Legs A last night, so that is nine days in a row, 9 to 17 November. Nothing is broken: all 20 sets done in 45 minutes, leg press 220 for 8, 8, 8 (the card asked 210), leg curl 157.5 for 12 on all three, calf press 300 for 13 on all three, every other lift on its card. If you train today anyway, the Push B card has my numbers on it.

The program changed today (version 14), and the week stays at 119 sets. The loads have been right; where the sets went was not. Counted the way the app counts (1 for a main mover, one half for a helper), side delts, which set shoulder width on stage, were getting 8 sets a week while rear delts got 15.5. So: lateral raises go to four sets on each push day; the reverse pec deck comes off Push A and stays on Push B; leg press on Legs A goes to four sets and the Legs A leg extension to three, because quads were level with hamstrings (the next Legs A is about a week away, so those two first run in full after the lighter week); one reverse curl set comes off Pull B. Counted the same way, side delts are now 10 and rear delts 12.5, so side delts are still behind; the first two four-set lateral nights decide the next step. No lift is swapped. Sessions are now Push A 17 sets, Pull A 19, Legs A 22, Push B 21, Pull B 20, Legs B 20.

Push B numbers (19 November, or today if you train): shoulder press 50 for 10 on all four. Chest press 165 for 10 on all three, one weight, no lighter first set; this is the heavier chest press day (8 to 10 reps), and Push A uses the same machine for 10 to 12, which is why the two cards can show different numbers. Lateral raise 17.5 for 13, 13, 13, 12, four sets. High-to-low crossover 30.5 for 15, 13. Reverse pec deck 97.5 for 13 on all three. Rope pushdown 50.5 for 12 on all three. Overhead dumbbell triceps extension, one dumbbell in both hands behind your head: 60 for 12, 12, what you logged in this slot on 12 November under its old name.

Your notes are answered one by one under this brief, all twelve of them back to 30 October. The short version of the big one, whether the science supports the set counts: roughly 10 to 20 hard sets a week per muscle for a trained lifter is what the research supports; your week was inside that except side delts, which were under it; rear delts and forearms were inside it but taking sets the stage scores less, and those sets moved to side delts and quads today. Your question last night about feet high on one leg press day: no, both stay low, because low is the quad position and quads are what needed more.

Show prep, 14 weeks out: the plan is written out under this brief. Prep starts 9 December after the lighter week (from 25 November) and assessment week (from 2 December). Four things are missing that I need in order to coach it: a bodyweight (none logged since 23 August), your division, photos or a waist measurement, and whether someone else sets your diet. The bodyweight is the urgent one: from 9 December there are just under 12 weeks, enough for roughly 12 to 23 lb at a sensible pace, and without a current weight I cannot tell whether that is enough or whether fat loss has to start sooner. I would also like to know whether this gym has a standing or seated calf machine.

Still open: if the shrug's fourth set is missing again on the next Pull B, that card drops to three sets. Your logs are still stamped Meso 3, week 8; if the phase at the top of the app is locked, the lighter week on 25 November will not start by itself, and "Automatic (by date)" clears the lock.

Today: rest. An easy 20 to 30 minute walk or bike ride is fine. Eat and sleep like it is a training day.

block.why: Today, 18 November, is set as a rest day. Nothing has broken: on 17 November all 20 sets were done in 45 minutes and every lift went up or met its card (leg press 220 for 8, 8, 8 against a card of 210, leg curl 157.5 for 12 on all three, calf press 300 for 13 on all three). It is week 4 of 4 of the build block restarted at the New York gym on 28 October. The build runs to 24 November, the lighter week is 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, and the show is 103 days away. The block is doing what a build block should: every lift logged at this gym since 9 November went up or held its weight. The loads were right; where the sets were spent was not. Version 14 today moves sets toward what the stage scores without adding any: side delts 8 to 10 counted sets (a fourth lateral set on each push day), quads 13 to 15 (a fourth leg press set and a third leg extension set on Legs A, which first run in full after the lighter week), paid for by rear delts 15.5 to 12.5 (reverse pec deck off Push A) and forearms 11 to 10 (one reverse curl set). The week stays at 119 sets: Push A 17, Pull A 19, Legs A 22, Push B 21, Pull B 20, Legs B 20. No lift is swapped, so the December assessment still compares like with like. The ranges are restated on one counting rule and every muscle sits inside its range on that rule. If you rest today the days run Push B 19 November, Pull B 20, Legs B 21, Push A 22, Pull A 23, rest 24 November; if you train today each moves one day earlier. At 25 November the lighter week runs as the calendar sets it: about 60 percent of the sets, weights about 20 percent lighter. prep.plan: Three weeks come before prep. This week (to 24 November) is the last build week, with the numbers on the cards. The week of 25 November is the lighter week: the calendar sets it at about 60 percent of the usual sets with weights about 20 percent lighter, and nothing taken near failure. The week of 2 December is assessment: each main lift is run at its current weight for its best reps, and the starting bodyweight is set. Prep starts on 9 December and runs just under 12 weeks. Weeks 1 to 4 (9 December to 5 January): the same lifts, sets and weights as now; in prep, holding reps at the same weight while bodyweight comes down is the win. Weeks 5 to 8 (6 January to 2 February): the weights stay, and if recovery slips, sets come off what the stage scores least (rear delts, forearms, traps, the hip machines) before anything comes off side delts, back, chest, arms, quads or calves. Weeks 9 to 11 (3 to 21 February): the same, no new lifts, no set taken to a grinding rep. The final week (22 February to 1 March): about half the sets, with the last hard leg session early in the week. Fat loss is paced at about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, which at your last logged 207 lb is about 1 to 2 lb a week. It is checked by the weekly average of morning weigh-ins: less than half a percent for two weeks running means food or daily walking has to change; more than one percent with reps dropping means it is too fast. From 9 December to the show is just under 12 weeks, so at that pace the most that can come off is roughly 12 to 23 lb from 207. Whether that is enough is not something I can tell: the last weigh-in in the log is 23 August, and there are no photos and no division. If more than that has to come off, the only slack is the three weeks before 9 December, which is why the weigh-in matters this week and not in December.
prep.next_step: A morning bodyweight in the log this week (the Bodyweight button on the workout screen). The first review after it says whether a 9 December start leaves enough weeks, or whether fat loss has to start during the lighter week from 25 November.

answers.note: WHAT THE FUCK. YOU GAVE ME TWO DIPS EXERCISES???!?!
answers.answer: The card was wrong. A slot you had renamed Dips on 28 October sat on the same Push B card as the assisted dips, so you were shown dips twice. The second dips slot came off on 1 November and dips now live on Push A only. What stops it happening again: since 17 November the check that every review must pass before it reaches the app reads tonight's card by the names you will see, and refuses any card that shows one movement twice.

Because rows are what build back thickness, and this row is half of all the rowing in your week: four sets here and four of the chest-supported row on Pull B. Counted the way the app counts (1 for a main mover, one half for a helper) your upper back gets 18 sets a week, inside the 10 to 20 the research supports for a trained lifter. The row is going up on four sets (105 for 10, then 105 for 12, then 112.5 for 10 on all four), so you are recovering from it. Four stays.

answers.note: What the fuck is this weight suggestion..you are absolutely braindead. One more mistake and you're getting fired
answers.answer: The card was wrong and that was my error. You had logged this slot as a leg extension on 30 October, the app kept your name on the card, and the review went on prescribing from the smith squat's starting weight underneath it, so you saw Leg Extension with a squat number. On 10 November the slot became a leg extension in its own name, starting from your own numbers; on 14 November it ran as itself at 157.5 for 10, 10, 10. What stops it happening again: every morning the review now reads the name each card will show and the lift the number comes from, and they have to match.

answers.note: Four sets? Does the science support any of your set counts?
answers.answer: Yes for all but one, and that one changes today along with two I am moving for a different reason. The research on weekly hard sets per muscle (Schoenfeld, Ogborn and Krieger 2017, and the studies since) puts growth at roughly 10 to 20 sets a week for a trained lifter, with more toward the top for the muscles you most need to bring up. Counted one way for every muscle (1 for a main mover, one half for a helper), your week was: chest 18, lats 18, upper back 19.5, biceps 18, triceps 16.5, hamstrings 14, quads 13, all inside that. One was not: side delts at 8 were under it. Rear delts at 15.5 and forearms at 11 were inside the research range; they come down because the stage scores them less than side delts and quads, and the sets were needed there. Today side delts go to 10, quads to 15, rear delts to 12.5 and forearms to 10, with the week still at 119 sets. The earlier reviews also argued some counts with direct sets and others with the counted number; from today every range uses the counted number and each muscle shows both.

answers.note: It seems like every day we do lateral raises. Do you know what you're doing?
answers.answer: You were right about how often: laterals were on three of the six days, and since 14 November they are on the two push days only. What I got wrong was the response. I read your question as a limit and cut side delts to 6 direct sets a week (8 counted with the half credit from the shoulder press), the smallest share of any muscle the stage scores, when they are the muscle that sets shoulder width. Today lateral raises go to four sets on each push day: 8 direct, 10 counted, still on two days. The lift is going up (15 for 15s on 12 November, 17.5 for 12s on 15 November).

You should not have been. 150 for 10, 10 on 4 November was already the top of Push B's 8 to 10, so the 12 November card should have moved up and it held you at 150 for the first set. You went to 157.5 and 165 for 9 yourself. Tonight's Push B card is 165 on all three sets.

answers.note: Do you just blindly apply my replacement exercises going forward for all eternity?
answers.answer: Until 14 November, yes, and that was wrong. The app keeps a name you type over a slot and prints it on every later card at that gym, and no review was deciding whether the swap should stay. On 14 November this slot became its own lift (the overhead dumbbell triceps extension), which clears the old name. From now on each morning's review reads the names tonight's card will show, and a replacement either becomes the slot with a reason or the slot goes back; it is no longer left to ride.

answers.note: Is it deliberate that we aren't doing any direct tricep work in this workout?
answers.answer: It was not designed that way; it happened in two steps. The rope pushdown came off Push A on 13 October to make room for lateral raises, and the overhead cable extension became dips on 1 November because you did dips in that slot on 28 October and the swap was adopted. I am keeping it, for this reason: dips load the triceps as a main mover, three sets, and with the pushdown and overhead extension on Push B and the help from every press, triceps get 16.5 counted sets a week (8 of them direct), in the upper half of the 10 to 20 range. What is thin is isolation work: 5 sets a week, all on Push B. If the pushdown and the extension stop going up, the first move is a triceps isolation lift back on Push A.

answers.note: Wtf why are you saying stalled?!?! Why are the weights here going up and down session to session. What the fuck are you doing
answers.answer: Two separate things. The "stalled" label was wrong: the app was comparing this gym's chest press with a different gym's machine. That was a bug in the app; it was fixed in version 93 on 17 November and the label is gone from this lift. The up and down is real and is on purpose, but the card never told you why: the same machine is on both push days with different reps. Push B presses it second for 8 to 10 (165 for 9 on 12 November); Push A presses it after four sets of incline for 10 to 12 (157.5 for 12s on 15 November). That split is the one you accepted on 23 July. From today each chest press card says which day it is and why its number differs, and there is one weight on all three sets.

answers.note: We should be doing this exercise every push day?
answers.answer: No. It comes off Push A today and stays on Push B. Counted with half credit for helper work, rear delts were getting 15.5 sets a week against 8 for side delts, which is backwards for a stage. The slot on Push A becomes a fourth set of lateral raises; that makes it 12.5 against 10, closer but not yet the right way round.

answers.note: Legs a and b both have feet low. Should one have feet high?
answers.answer: No, both stay feet low. Feet low bends the knee more and puts the work on the quads; feet high moves it to glutes and hamstrings. Your hamstrings and glutes are already at the top of their ranges from the deadlift, RDL and two leg curl days (14 and 13.5 counted sets), and quads are what the front poses are scored on, which is why quads go from 13 to 15 sets today. The two leg press days differ by reps, not foot position: Legs A is 8 to 10 (220 for 8s on 17 November), Legs B is 10 to 12.

changes_today.why: You asked on 15 November whether this exercise should be on every push day. No, and it comes off Push A today. Rear delts had 10 direct sets a week (this machine on both push days, face pulls on both pull days) and they also get help from every row and pulldown: 15.5 sets a week once that help is counted at half. Side delts, which set how wide your shoulders look on stage, had 6 direct and 8 counted the same way. That is the wrong way round for a physique that is going to be judged, and it is what the 17 November audit of this program found. The reverse pec deck stays on Push B, where you did 97.5 for 12, 12, 12 on 12 November. Rear delts go to 7 direct sets a week, 12.5 with the half credit, inside the range. Counted that way side delts go from 8 to 10 today, so they are still behind rear delts; the gap went from 7.5 sets to 2.5, and the review after the first two four-set lateral nights decides the rest. On 17 November I wrote that this lift stays on both push days on purpose; the audit is the new fact since then. Push A goes from 19 sets to 17 once the fourth lateral set below is added.

A fourth set of lateral raises on Push A, in the place the reverse pec deck left. On 23 August you asked whether four sets was right for such a small muscle and said you would do it if I was sure. I am sure, and the program should have said so then instead of cutting the set. The research on how many hard sets a muscle needs each week to grow (Schoenfeld, Ogborn and Krieger 2017, and the studies since) lands at roughly 10 to 20 for a trained lifter, and a small muscle does not need fewer. Side delts were getting 6 direct sets, 8 with the half credit from the shoulder press. Four sets on each push day makes 8 direct and 10 counted, the bottom of that range, for the muscle that decides shoulder width on stage. The lift is going up (17.5 for 12, 12, 12 on 15 November after 12.5 for 14, 13, 13 on 9 November), so you are recovering from what it gets now.

A fourth set of lateral raises on Push B too, for the same reason as Push A: side delts go from 6 direct sets a week to 8, and from 8 to 10 with the half credit from the shoulder press. Laterals stay on two days a week, the two push days. The cable raise that came off Pull A on 14 November stays off, so this is more work on the days you already do them, not more days. Push B goes from 20 sets to 21. You did 15 for 15, 15, 15 here on 12 November and 17.5 for 12, 12, 12 on Push A on 15 November.

A fourth set of leg press on Legs A. Quads had 13 sets a week, level with hamstrings, and quads are what the front poses are scored on. Every quad lift went up on 17 November: leg press 220 for 8, 8, 8 (the card asked 210), leg extension 157.5 for 12, 12, split squat 25 for 8, 8. Legs A took 45 minutes for all 20 sets that night, so there is room for more. With the third leg extension set below, quads go to 15 sets a week and Legs A to 22 sets. The whole week stays at 119 sets, because the same version takes four off rear delts and forearms (three reverse pec deck sets on Push A, one reverse curl set). The next Legs A falls on 24 or 25 November, at the edge of the lighter week, so the first Legs A at the full four sets is likely the one after it.

A third set of leg extensions on Legs A, the same count as Legs B. This is the second of the two added quad sets (see the leg press change): quads go from 13 sets a week to 15. You did 157.5 for 12, 12 on 17 November, the bottom of this slot's 12 to 15, after 150 for 13, 13 on 11 November.

One set comes off the reverse curl on Pull B. Forearms had 6 direct sets a week (hammer curl and this) and 11 with half credit from the dumbbell curl, the shrug and the RDL: more than side delts were getting. Forearms count for little on stage next to shoulders and quads, so this set is one of the four that pay for the added lateral and quad sets and keep the week at 119 (the other three are the reverse pec deck on Push A). Forearms go to 5 direct and 10 counted; biceps to 10 direct and 17 counted. The lift itself is fine (32.5 for 10, then 37.5 for 10, 10 on 13 November) and keeps its weight. Pull B goes from 21 sets to 20.

You asked on 10 November whether the science supports any of these set counts, and the 17 November audit found the reviews had been counting sets two different ways to suit the argument. This fixes the ranges to one rule. Every range is now for the number the app prints: a set counts 1 for each muscle doing the main work and one half for each muscle helping. The old ranges were written for direct sets only and then judged against the counted number, which is why six muscles read as over. The ranges come from the research on weekly hard sets per muscle (Schoenfeld, Ogborn and Krieger 2017): roughly 10 to 20 for a trained lifter. What a stage scores sits at 10 or 12 up to 20: side delts, chest, lats, upper back, biceps, triceps, quads; calves 8 to 16. What matters less sits lower: rear delts 6 to 14, forearms 4 to 10, traps, lower back, abductors and abs unchanged. Adductors go to 2 to 8: two of their sets are direct and the rest is help given on the leg press and split squat, which the fourth leg press set adds to. Front delts go to 6 to 16 because all of their work is a by-product of chest and shoulder pressing; no set is there only for them. The side-delt floor goes from 6 back up to 10: I lowered it on 14 November to fit a cap I had read into your two questions about laterals, and a question is not a cap. With today's set changes every muscle sits inside its range on this one count. Two scored muscles sit at the bottom of theirs: side delts at 10 and calves at 9.

The remaining gap is dated, not closed: a third lateral day today would undo the 14 November change with no night logged at four sets, so the 23 November review decides after the 19 and 22 November lateral nights; calves get a second lift at the 2 December review.

findings.finding: The answer to the 15 November Push A triceps question began “Yes, deliberate”, but the change log shows it came from two earlier swaps (pushdown off on 13 October, dips adopted on 1 November), not from a design.

findings.finding: The answer on whether the science supports the set counts said rear delts at 15.5 and forearms at 11 were not supported; both are inside the 10 to 20 range it cites, and only side delts at 8 were outside.
findings.why: The answer and the brief now say only side delts were outside the research range, and that rear delts and forearms come down as a priority call for the stage.

findings.finding: The low-to-high crossover plan said 15 for 12 next; this gym’s cables have moved in 1.5 lb steps in his log, so the step above 12.5 is probably 14, and 15 may not exist on the stack.
